Wait, let me re-read §152(c). A brother IS a qualifying child under §152(c)(2)(B) - "a brother, sister, stepbrother, or stepsister of the taxpayer or a descendant of any such relative."

So Bob IS a qualifying child of Alice.

For head of household status (§2(b)(1)(A)), the person must maintain household with a "qualifying child" - which Bob is. So Alice qualifies as head of household.

Phaseout threshold for head of household is §68(b)(1)(B) = $275,000
Alice's AGI = $260,932 < $275,000, so NO phaseout applies.

$260,932 - $4,400 - $4,000 = $252,532

Regarding the standard deduction limitation for dependents in §63(c)(5), it doesn't apply here because the restriction only affects the basic standard deduction, and Alice as the head of household would claim the full $4,400 anyway.
